programme.title: Crafting Cabinet Doors: Materials & Cutting Techniques
programme.desc: In the episode the craftsman guides viewers through essential techniques and considerations for crafting cabinet doors with precision and efficiency. He begins by stressing the importance of wood selection, advising against woods with prominent grain patterns like oak, which are unsuitable for door frames. Instead, he recommends using straight-grained pieces from the edges of the wood or opting for materials like MDF, birch, or maple for paint-grade projects due to their smooth surfaces and availability in large sheets. The craftsman demonstrates how to prepare materials for construction, including ripping pieces for frames and face frames, and discusses the suitability of poplar for practice due to its affordability and ease of machining. When it comes to door panels, he explains the careful use of plywood and the importance of adjusting grooves precisely for optimal fit. He showcases the use of a dado head to create tenons that snugly fit into these grooves, ensuring strong and gap-free assembly. Techniques for creating specific door styles are highlighted, such as using half-lap joints adjusted on the table saw for flush fits. The craftsman emphasizes marking and consistent cuts to avoid errors, crucial for achieving perfect joints in door frame assembly. He demonstrates assembly steps and discusses adding decorative pegs for both aesthetic appeal and structural integrity, particularly useful for heavier doors like those with leaded glass panels. Throughout the episode, the craftsman underscores the use of templates for ensuring consistent shapes, particularly useful for cathedral-style doors. He employs a band saw and router table with double-sided tape to achieve precision in shaping components, emphasizing careful setup and sequential cuts for optimal woodworking results. Overall, the episode provides comprehensive guidance on wood selection, tool adjustment, joint creation, and assembly techniques, empowering woodworkers to create high-quality cabinet doors effectively.

programme.title: Fashion Inside and Out - The Late 1940's
programme.desc: As the war ended, women wore more tailored garments and pants. Fabric was readily available and flounces and drape became important design details to soften the masculine look. programme.title: Crafting Cabinet Doors: Materials & Cutting Techniques
programme.desc: In the episode the craftsman guides viewers through essential techniques and considerations for crafting cabinet doors with precision and efficiency. He begins by stressing the importance of wood selection, advising against woods with prominent grain patterns like oak, which are unsuitable for door frames. Instead, he recommends using straight-grained pieces from the edges of the wood or opting for materials like MDF, birch, or maple for paint-grade projects due to their smooth surfaces and availability in large sheets. The craftsman demonstrates how to prepare materials for construction, including ripping pieces for frames and face frames, and discusses the suitability of poplar for practice due to its affordability and ease of machining. When it comes to door panels, he explains the careful use of plywood and the importance of adjusting grooves precisely for optimal fit. He showcases the use of a dado head to create tenons that snugly fit into these grooves, ensuring strong and gap-free assembly. Techniques for creating specific door styles are highlighted, such as using half-lap joints adjusted on the table saw for flush fits. The craftsman emphasizes marking and consistent cuts to avoid errors, crucial for achieving perfect joints in door frame assembly. He demonstrates assembly steps and discusses adding decorative pegs for both aesthetic appeal and structural integrity, particularly useful for heavier doors like those with leaded glass panels. Throughout the episode, the craftsman underscores the use of templates for ensuring consistent shapes, particularly useful for cathedral-style doors. He employs a band saw and router table with double-sided tape to achieve precision in shaping components, emphasizing careful setup and sequential cuts for optimal woodworking results. Overall, the episode provides comprehensive guidance on wood selection, tool adjustment, joint creation, and assembly techniques, empowering woodworkers to create high-quality cabinet doors effectively.

programme.title: Nature-Inspired Crafts: Wooden Rope Seat & Slab Wood Coffee Table
programme.desc: In the episode "Easy Projects with Native Materials," the focus is on crafting robust furniture using natural materials, bringing joy to woodworking enthusiasts. The project kicks off with a stool build using one-inch dowels for rails and sturdy legs crafted from one-and-a-half-inch square pieces. A standout feature is the woven seat, initially demonstrated with bundling twine but showcased with Cecil rope for its natural charm and durability. The construction process begins meticulously, drilling precise holes using a drill press for consistent alignment. Offset holes on adjacent faces accommodate the rails snugly, while chamfered ends prevent any interference during assembly. Dry-fitting ensures all components fit seamlessly before applying glue, guaranteeing a sturdy final product. After assembly, the stool is clamped securely to maintain square alignment and left to dry before sanding and finishing bring out the wood's natural beauty. The seat weaving process is a highlight, with the speaker demonstrating how to wrap Cecil rope around the frame in a precise pattern, creating a durable and visually appealing seat. Throughout, the importance of precision and the handy use of pliers for control during weaving are emphasized. The episode also explores comparisons between stools made from different materials, celebrating the diversity of woodworking choices. Transitioning to a coffee table project, the speaker selects wood pieces with a striking blue stain for added visual interest. Techniques for drilling and joint fitting are expertly demonstrated, ensuring the table frame is not just sturdy but also artistically crafted. Challenges encountered, such as uneven surfaces or knots in the tabletop, are met with practical solutions, including finishing tips with Danish oil for a natural, lustrous look. Throughout the tutorial, the joy of working with native materials and the satisfaction of creating beautiful, enduring furniture pieces shine through, making it a delightful watch for woodworking enthusiasts of all skill levels.

programme.desc: Is Joseph Haydn's music boring? Not at all, say Paavo Järvi and the musicians of the Deutsche Kammerphilharmonie Bremen. On their musical journey through Haydn's symphonic works, they discover new and surprising things.

programme.title: DocFilm
programme.desc: More than 140 years after its invention, the car remains a source of fascination for many people. In Germany, for example, there are more vehicles on the road than ever before. For some, the car is a cult object. But it also deeply polarizing.
programme.sub-title: My Holy Car - An Obsession made in Germany - Part 1

programme.title: Combat Forces
programme.desc: Artillery is known as the hammer of the battlefield because of the awesome firepower it can bring down on an enemy. Imagine if that same firepower could be mobile and dropped behind enemy lines? That is the premise behind airborne artillery, a specialized force charged with supporting soldiers with long distance firepower. We go to Fort Bragg NC to learn about this unique warfare discipline.

programme.title: Conducting Life
programme.desc: Filmed over seven years, the film follows the improbable journey of conductor Roderick Cox and his quest to succeed in the highly competitive field of orchestral conducting. This profession has traditionally overlooked musicians of color.

programme.title: Frontline Fashion
programme.desc: Frontline Fashion is an award-winning docu-series that follows the most talented emerging fashion designers from all over the globe

programme.title: The Power of Play
programme.desc: Lizards do it. Even fish do it. The animal world is showing us why play is a serious matter. Through a combination of ongoing experiments, reconstructed experiments and guided observation. The Power of Play reveals surprising truths about play in the natural world. Scientists from Europe, the United States and Canada, many of them pioneers in the field, offer convincing evidence that play is not to be taken lightly. In fact, it has the power to make animals and humans smarter, healthier and more likely to survive.

programme.title: Fight Club London
programme.desc: Fight Club London looks at one of the world's fastest growing sports, Mixed Martial Arts. Three fighters prepare for upcoming cage fights. A 14 year boy, a fully-fledged pro, and an Indian girl who wants to make her cage debut before she gets married. What’s the true reality behind this sport?

programme.title: Who Made You?
programme.desc: Artificial intellignce is reaching our mental and physical existence like never before. The film leads us to the world of cyborgs, sex robots and androids. It challenges us to face our values, ethics and rethink our position. To keep our humanistic values on board with the development, we have to be awake - tight now. Eye-opening scences from Finland, Spain, Swedenm Geece amd Japan reveals the on-going processes and development on a global level. The guide in our stimulating journey is a young aspiring Dr Michael Laakasuo who is making pioneering research on the field of ethics and AI. He stresses that machine-ethics should not be left behind in the technological development. The film asks what the development of AI means to us as human beings. What does it mean for humanity, community, and how it will affect our perception of human? What are the values we want to hold on to?

programme.title: Tent City Hollywood
programme.desc: Explore Hollywood's streets over 9 months-unchanged struggles, untold stories. A raw look at the encampments in Los Angeles.

programme.title: 24 Hours At Gound Zero
programme.desc: An extraordinary inside look at the evolution of the World Trade Center horror, experienced through the eyes and the voices of people at the scene including a policeman, a fireman and an EMS worker who were among the first to arrive at ground zero. Our cameras wer the first on hand and we have some of the most definitive footage from the event of its time. This program aired on MSNBC.

programme.title: Town Of Glory
programme.desc: As Russia faces growing international isolation, loyalists within the 30 million-strong Russian diaspora are dedicated to defending, supporting and promoting Putin overseas. Vladimir Putin has made it clear that he wants Russia to reclaim its former glory: across the globe.

programme.title: Gun Shot Wound
programme.desc: Gun Shot Wound takes a hard look at routine gun violence in America through the eyes of its trauma surgeons. The film examines the crisis through a public health lens and highlights hospital-based violence intervention programs designed to combat the epidemic. Every day in the United States, an average of 318 people are shot - about 116,000 victims each year. Most aren't involved in mass shootings, instead they're caught in the web of routine, almost invisioble, gun violence. Gun Shot Wound show what really happens when someone gets shot and highlights how physicians and hospitals are not just treating patients, but going above and beyond to prevent gun violence.

programme.title: The House In Arguello
programme.desc: Valentina Llorens’ uncle disappeared during the military dictatorship in Argentina. When his remains are discovered she starts researching the family’s history. Her grandmother was active in the civil movement “Mothers of Plaza de Mayo” and her mother political prisoner.

programme.title: Combat Forces
programme.desc: Today, as in the past, one of the best means to enter combat is with allies. Today military forces work together to fight enemies in places such as Iraq and Afghanistan. This cooperation and understanding of each other operating procedures are critical to their success in battle.

programme.title: Balika
programme.desc: Dipendra and Sushmita are two Napali orphans living in an orphanage in Kathmandu. One day, Dipendra's family contacts him and they invite him to travel to his hometown. Sushmita decides that when she grows up she want to be a nurse.

programme.title: Birdhill
programme.desc: Eva’s childhood home, Bratislava’s Birdhill, was once Maria Theresa's vineyards and forest. Now, cranes and excavators dominate. In her film, she meets current inhabitants, each living a different dream of this charismatic place. Yet, though they share the hill, they cannot unite to halt the ruthless, rapid construction transforming their home beyond recognition.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: Discover China is a documentary series shot in conjunction with the Chinese Ministry of Culture and China Central Television, including footage of never before seen locations and recreations of historical events. It was shot by BBC film crews over a four year period. At the foot of Tai Mountain sits an enigma, a temple that bears a striking resemblance to an Imperial palace. It was built by a brazen emperor, who ignored his country's desparation, and built this lavish shrine to bolster his status as the sole ruler.

programme.title: MOMA - Moments of Modern Art
programme.desc: Moments of Modern Art is a special feature, showcasing incredible works of art and design. From sculptures to tattoos, photography to smartphone art, learn what inspires artists and designers, have a glance into the world of contemporary art and be uplifted by the dedication they have to their craft. With stories from all over the world, this is more than a show about art and design; this is a way of living!

programme.title: Haunted New Orleans
programme.desc: In the heart of the Big Easy, restless spirits reveal chilling tales-voodoo curses, spectral jazz, and forgotten secrets. Ghosts, cryptids, and eerie history explore the supernatural secrets of New Orleans in this chilling documentary.

programme.title: State of Rodeo
programme.desc: State of Rodeo follows a diverse group of characters who participate in the sport of rodeo and explores the heritage of the cattle industry within the state of Florida and it's influence on western culture from the time of Ponce De Leon's first settlement to present day cowboys and cowgirls. Rodeo still fascinates to this day, the heritage of this sport's tradition is one of the founding industries of our nation and most people don't know that Florida played an integral role in this history.

programme.title: In The Executioner's Shadow
programme.desc: The death penalty is one of America's most polarizing practices. Meet an executioner, a bombing victim struggling with justice, and parents whose child was murdered, in this doc, exploring capital punishment.

programme.title: We Don’t Do Charity
programme.desc: Across the Global South social entrepreneurs, civil society organisations, and grass roots NGOs are rejecting the ‘white saviourism’ of rich countries in favour of sustainable development programmes designed by them, for their own communities.

programme.title: Jaffa: A Guide to Gentrification
programme.desc: Jaffa, once a major port in the Middle East and the sister city of Tel Aviv, “the most expensive city in the world” per The Economist, has grown into an international tourist center, a coveted destination and last but not least a true real estate gem.

programme.title: On The Inside Of a Military Dictatorship
programme.desc:
“On the Inside of a Military Dictatorship” takes its audience back to when the military made their master plan for a so-called disciplined democracy in Myanmar and wrote a very scripted role for their enemy no. 1; Aung San Suu Kyi. In a dramatic way, the film builds the character- and story set-up to take us anew into the crisis we know from the news – however, with a radically different perspective. The story is based on unique acces to the key players in this complicated reality, including Aung San Suu Kyi and previous President Thein Sein.
It’s the story of how power struggles unfold and how political enemies can end up being closer than the ones they claim to fight for: the people. The audience gets deeper and deeper into this complex world of power driven by peculiar characters and even astrology.

programme.desc: Slab City is a squatter community in the Sonoran Desert and 'the last free place in America'. Their closest neighbours are the Marine Corps, who practice aerial bombing in the area.

programme.title: The River Between Us
programme.desc: A River Between Us tells the story of the oldest and most bitterly disputed water war in the West today. The film's primary focus is the struggle for justice on the Klamath River, where forty years of bad blood between the local farmers, ranchers, Native Tribes, members of the Tea Party, state politicians and federal government have created one of this country's worst environmental crises. Most importantly, as part of the largest restoration project in American history, A River Between Us provides the solution to ending this generations-old conflict: in order to save a river, you must first heal a people.

programme.title: Elliott Erwitt, Silence Sounds Good
programme.desc:
Directed by Erwitt's previous assistant, a documentary about the Magnum photographer, tirelessly dedicated to his art, and, in his own words, "very serious about not being serious".
Director

programme.title: Meltdown in Dixie
programme.desc: In the wake of the 2015 Charleston Massacre, a battle erupts in Orangeburg, South Carolina between the Sons of Confederate Veterans and an ice cream shop owner forced to fly the Confederate flag in his parking lot. MELTDOWN IN DIXIE explores the broader role of Confederate symbolism in 21st century America and the lingering racial oppression which these symbols help maintain.

programme.title: Idomeni
programme.desc: Idomeni is both a place suspended in time, and a film shaped by scenes from the parallel lives of adults and children in the camp. The children do not go to school but live in their own world and take care of each other, having little contact with their surroundings. The film catches their bubble and shows: they are tomorrow's Europe. It is a place where you are suspended in time. You cannot move forward and you cannot go back. You are confined. But it is not a prison, it is a refugee camp. Refugee camps are usually located far away from the rest of society and they become like worlds of their own. This is a film about life in the camps. The film does not explore the dramatic events of the journey but the seemingly still and slowed down moments in the camps.

programme.title: Birds Without Wings
programme.desc: Two adults who grew up in the slums of Delhi strive to give new wings to the kids bounded by the shackles of poverty, drugs, and society.

programme.title: War Peace
programme.desc: War/Peace documentary film is re-introducing the radical student activists from the late 60s. Ex-leaders of The Weather Underground movement Bill Ayers and Bernardine Dohrn. For decades the government and press have tried their best to silence them. This film will serve as an historical reminder of what happened the last time a group of young minds planned to take over an unpopular government in Washington.

programme.title: PostCard From Afghanistan
programme.desc: Comedian Mike King faces a stand-up gig like none other when asked to perform for American troops based in Afghanistan. King also meets with Kiwi soldiers situated in Kabul, Bagram, and Bamyan and talks about how they are helping rebuild and provide security in the war-torn country. During his journey, he learns about life in Afghanistan for these soldiers and the roles they play in the decades-long war. A siren signaling an "indirect airstrike" causes King and his team to scramble for shelter as they experience first-hand terror of war.

programme.title: Music For Elephants
programme.desc: An incredible, unique and moving documentary about a concert pianist, who plays music to blind, injured and orphaned elephants with amazing results. At a sanctuary on the shores of the iconic River Kwai in Thailand, Paul Barton plays the works of world’s greatest composers to endangered Asian elephants and reveals their secret love of music.

programme.title: Grain: Analog Renaissance
programme.desc: Today, the art world and beyond is obsessed with shooting analog. Whether it’s a fashion house seeking to bring a new edge to their creative work, an amateur perusing eBay for the perfect vintage Polaroid, or an influencer attempting to capture a comforting retro aesthetic on social media, analog photography has piqued the interest of people everywhere. Is this resurgence a backlash against digital photography? Is it just a trend perpetuated by our desire for authentically in an increasingly superficial world? Or is it something else entirely? We explore the stories of those committed to using film in modern day photography

programme.title: PostCard From Afghanistan
programme.desc: Comedian Mike King faces a stand-up gig like none other when asked to perform for American troops based in Afghanistan. King also meets with Kiwi soldiers situated in Kabul, Bagram, and Bamyan and talks about how they are helping rebuild and provide security in the war-torn country. During his journey, he learns about life in Afghanistan for these soldiers and the roles they play in the decades-long war. A siren signaling an "indirect airstrike" causes King and his team to scramble for shelter as they experience first-hand terror of war.

programme.title: Music For Elephants
programme.desc: An incredible, unique and moving documentary about a concert pianist, who plays music to blind, injured and orphaned elephants with amazing results. At a sanctuary on the shores of the iconic River Kwai in Thailand, Paul Barton plays the works of world’s greatest composers to endangered Asian elephants and reveals their secret love of music.

programme.title: Grain: Analog Renaissance
programme.desc: Today, the art world and beyond is obsessed with shooting analog. Whether it’s a fashion house seeking to bring a new edge to their creative work, an amateur perusing eBay for the perfect vintage Polaroid, or an influencer attempting to capture a comforting retro aesthetic on social media, analog photography has piqued the interest of people everywhere. Is this resurgence a backlash against digital photography? Is it just a trend perpetuated by our desire for authentically in an increasingly superficial world? Or is it something else entirely? We explore the stories of those committed to using film in modern day photography

programme.title: MOMA - Moments of Modern Art
programme.desc: Moments of Modern Art is a special feature, showcasing incredible works of art and design. From sculptures to tattoos, photography to smartphone art, learn what inspires artists and designers, have a glance into the world of contemporary art and be uplifted by the dedication they have to their craft. With stories from all over the world, this is more than a show about art and design; this is a way of living!

programme.title: Blame Game
programme.desc: Blame Game explores the challenges but also the possible solutions - some very simple - that could reduce waste, take advantage of an impressive skill-set, alleviate poverty and help our environment.

programme.title: Escape From Room 18
programme.desc: John Daly, an ex-Neo Nazi, fled to Israel when his gang tried to kill him for being Jewish. An old Skinhead friend finds John 25 years later and suggests they visit concentration camps in an effort to make amends for their past.

programme.title: Golden Age
programme.desc: Extravaganza and glamour lining up in an existential contest against isolation, slackening limbs and lethargy. With unique access behind the scences, the Palace in Miami is shown as a buzzing and luzurious senior living community, repeatedly voted "American's Number One". The seniors live in a world full of parties and entertainment, but the Palace is also a thrivin business.... Who said that old age has to be boring? Golden Age opens the doors to the Palace, a retirement home of the kind that you have never seen before, in Miami. Gildings, ostentatious chandeliers, marble floors; like a cross between a luxury hotel and an Americanised copy of Versailles, the place is presented by its developers as the most beautiful retirement home in the US. The residents here are pampered by an army of employees devoted to their every whim, in a oermanent party atmosphere. This abundance of luxury, extravagance and entertainment is nonetheless not enough to remove the anxieties of those who live there. Nor can it hide the intention of the investors for whome old age is above all source of income and a growing market. Golden Age takes us on a journey into this baroque universe which tries to suppress the fear of death through dollars, questioning, in a dizzying visual whirlwind, our relationship to old age in its most universal aspect.

programme.title: The Good Death
programme.desc:
Janette is terminally ill and wants to die in a dignified way. Muscular dystrophy, the illness that Janette suffers from, has affected her family for generations. Janette's mother was wheelchair bound for decades, a prisoner in her own body. Janette refuses to wait for death in unbearable pain and opts for physician-assisted suicide. Before leaving on her last journey she has to explain her intention to her family members and close friends. Her son Simon has also inherited this illness and, therefore, has much more sympathy for her decision than his sister Bridget. If no cure for this illness is found, he will face the same decision process as his mother. Both children try to convince Janette to postpone her death. Do we own our life or does it own us?
The film uses feature film techniques, and engaging characters and their stories interwoven with Janette’s testament.

programme.title: 300 Trillion The Debt Trap
programme.desc: The film explores the significance of our debt situation, looking at true stories behind the situation, from a debtors' prison in Mississippi to the world's most notoriously indebted country.

programme.title: 100 Million Views
programme.desc: We set out a mission to discover the secrets of what makes a video go viral. Along the way we meet with Youtube stars past and present, from the viral sensations of yesterday to the modern breed of Influencers who have fine-tuned the art of audience building, algorithmic tampering and fan engagement. But as our journey takes us deeper into the heart of the Youtube machine, questions emerge about how exactly this platform that was supposed to democratise entertainment, has evolved. With dark humour and caustic wit, 100 Million Views uncovers the truth about a platform that promised transparency and democracy, but hides an exploitative, censored and unaccountable underbelly.

programme.title: Haunted New Orleans
programme.desc: In the heart of the Big Easy, restless spirits reveal chilling tales-voodoo curses, spectral jazz, and forgotten secrets. Ghosts, cryptids, and eerie history explore the supernatural secrets of New Orleans in this chilling documentary.

programme.title: State of Rodeo
programme.desc: State of Rodeo follows a diverse group of characters who participate in the sport of rodeo and explores the heritage of the cattle industry within the state of Florida and it's influence on western culture from the time of Ponce De Leon's first settlement to present day cowboys and cowgirls. Rodeo still fascinates to this day, the heritage of this sport's tradition is one of the founding industries of our nation and most people don't know that Florida played an integral role in this history.

programme.title: In The Executioner's Shadow
programme.desc: The death penalty is one of America's most polarizing practices. Meet an executioner, a bombing victim struggling with justice, and parents whose child was murdered, in this doc, exploring capital punishment.

programme.title: We Don’t Do Charity
programme.desc: Across the Global South social entrepreneurs, civil society organisations, and grass roots NGOs are rejecting the ‘white saviourism’ of rich countries in favour of sustainable development programmes designed by them, for their own communities.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: Discover China is a documentary series shot in conjunction with the Chinese Ministry of Culture and China Central Television, including footage of never before seen locations and recreations of historical events. It was shot by BBC film crews over a four year period. At the foot of Tai Mountain sits an enigma, a temple that bears a striking resemblance to an Imperial palace. It was built by a brazen emperor, who ignored his country's desparation, and built this lavish shrine to bolster his status as the sole ruler.

programme.title: MOMA - Moments of Modern Art
programme.desc: Moments of Modern Art is a special feature, showcasing incredible works of art and design. From sculptures to tattoos, photography to smartphone art, learn what inspires artists and designers, have a glance into the world of contemporary art and be uplifted by the dedication they have to their craft. With stories from all over the world, this is more than a show about art and design; this is a way of living!

programme.title: Haunted New Orleans
programme.desc: In the heart of the Big Easy, restless spirits reveal chilling tales-voodoo curses, spectral jazz, and forgotten secrets. Ghosts, cryptids, and eerie history explore the supernatural secrets of New Orleans in this chilling documentary.

programme.title: State of Rodeo
programme.desc: State of Rodeo follows a diverse group of characters who participate in the sport of rodeo and explores the heritage of the cattle industry within the state of Florida and it's influence on western culture from the time of Ponce De Leon's first settlement to present day cowboys and cowgirls. Rodeo still fascinates to this day, the heritage of this sport's tradition is one of the founding industries of our nation and most people don't know that Florida played an integral role in this history.

programme.title: In The Executioner's Shadow
programme.desc: The death penalty is one of America's most polarizing practices. Meet an executioner, a bombing victim struggling with justice, and parents whose child was murdered, in this doc, exploring capital punishment.

It's More Fun in the Philippines
programme.desc: Alex and Mel continue their amazing tour of the Philippines. A tropical storm saves the girls from a scary challenge, and they visit the home of the smallest primates in the world.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Ellen Coughlan travels to one of the most famous southern States of America. Exploring the narrow Gulf Coastline of Alabama, she’s on a mission to see how sweet it is.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: A forbidden city that was built hundreds of miles away from the capital in Beijing, still stands today on the hills and crests of this mountain, its peak serves as a ladder to heaven. The mysteries of this now deserted structure, which served both a ruler and a deity, are slowly being revealed. Wudang Mountain stands, aloof, veiled in mysterious tales of ancient gods and rich in imperial history. Its ridges stretch, shrouded with clouds and mist all year round. Discover China brings you the Mystery of XuanWu, a riveting tale of the bond between an emperor and a god, the link between man and nature, and the story behind WuDang Mountain, and its mystifying peaks.

programme.title: Hiking Europe-The alpe Adria Tail
programme.desc: Esme continues her epic hike along the 750km Alpe Adria Trail, watching the sunrise from a mountain top, searching for garnets in a mine, and visiting an artist with a very strange technique.

programme.title: The Boat Show
programme.desc: Luxury sailing, power boats, water sports and a nautical lifestyle. This show is for anyone who dreams of owning a vboat, of a life aboard ship, of beautiful people and places, and super yachts.

programme.title: The Flying Chef
programme.desc: Located in the heart of the Coral Triangle, Raja Ampat is the most biologically diverse marine region in the world. Chef Nathan cooks local delicacies made from mussels and papeda.

programme.title: Escape To Paradise
programme.desc: The Caribbean has always been a dream destination for holidaymakers dreaming of that perfect getaway, and Antigua has long been a favourite for the British. Of course, it spent several centuries under British rule, and the connections endure in names such as Nelson’s Dockyard and English Harbour. Today though, it’s the 365 beaches, year round sunshine, and colourful cocktails that bring the visitors.

programme.title: Ellen's American Adventure
programme.desc: Experience modern Texas as Ellen Coughlan arrives at Wildcatter Ranch to experience the thrills of a true cowboy lifestyle. Then it’s onto the glitzy city of Dallas.

programme.title: It's More Fun in the Philippines
programme.desc: Liü and Mel set off to visit a secluded island with a hidden secret in a mountain cave. Liü dives on an old shipwreck, and Mel tries to teach her friend a traditional Asian game from her childhood.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join Alyse Edwards as she explores the beautiful Turkish town of Alacati. Located on Turkey’s west coast Alacati is stunning town, steeped in history. And with its vibrant culture Alacati certainly lives up to its reputation of being a trendy town with plenty of restaurants, shopping, historical sites and water sports.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: No one could have dreamed that beneath the fields of a slumbering village in Henan province, a dormant civilization was awaiting to be brought back to light. From the discovery of mysteriously etched and engraved bone fragments and tortoise shells, an age old era of China emerged from beneath the plowed fields. As archeological excavations began, an age old fear of grave robbers set in the surveyor’s heart , when the wall of an ancient tomb was finally exposed. As the arduous explorations continued, an age in China’s history was finally uncovered. Discover China unearths the secrets of the Underground City.

programme.title: Summer In The Black Forest
programme.desc: The Black Forest is a land of fairy tales, legends, and of course, gateaux, right? Well Liu Batchelor is on a mission to find out, and uncovers many diverse and unusual tourist options along the way.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join Alyse Edwards as she explores the beautiful Turkish town of Alacati. Located on Turkey’s west coast Alacati is stunning town, steeped in history. programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: No one could have dreamed that beneath the fields of a slumbering village in Henan province, a dormant civilization was awaiting to be brought back to light. From the discovery of mysteriously etched and engraved bone fragments and tortoise shells, an age old era of China emerged from beneath the plowed fields. As archeological excavations began, an age old fear of grave robbers set in the surveyor’s heart , when the wall of an ancient tomb was finally exposed. As the arduous explorations continued, an age in China’s history was finally uncovered. Discover China unearths the secrets of the Underground City.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Alyse Edwards continues her journey in the Turkish town of Alacati. Starting inland she explores some of the remains of ancient civilisations and experiences some incredible views of Alacati and the surrounding areas. After a brief stop off for some exquisite wine, she heads to the nearby coastal town of Cesme for some further exploring and puts herself to the test by having a go at the famous local sport of Wind Surfing.

programme.title: Discover China
programme.desc: In the remote, ancient villages of southern Anhui Province in southeast China, a breed of merchants emerged, altering and reshaping the face of China’s trade and commerce. Cast in to the tumultuous world of business at a tender, early age, these boys turned into some of China’s most successful traders, businessmen and merchants. With their legacy firmly secure in their centuries old lavish and opulent houses, and their illustrious careers recorded in the annals of history for posterity, these shrewd astute, and influential merchants helped shape China’s commercial past for centuries. Discover China follows in the footsteps of the famous Huizhou Merchants.

programme.title: Essence Of India
programme.desc:
Samira is all excited for the Tandoori Party.
The world loves to BBQ and India has some of the oldest forms – Tandoori cooking. Samira takes a fresh approach to Tandoori cuisine and the grill that goes back thousands of years.
The Episode starts off with a visit to a Street Tandoori hub that makes Kababs that have a cult following of their own. Samira ends up taking over grill, learns the art of Tandoori breads and how can any Tandoori feast be complete without the Pièce de résistance, The Tandoori Chicken and a Party!

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join Ellen Coughlan as she explores the iconic city of New Orleans. Nicknamed the “Big Easy”, it’s known for its round the clock nightlife, vibrant live-music scene, and a spicy, singular cuisine… reflecting its history as a melting pot of French, African and American cultures. New Orleans is famous for its Mardi Gras, where parades and street parties fill the city. It’s also home to the iconic Natchez Steamboat, the last completely steam powered paddleboat on the Mississippi River. The second part features more food, some cocktail making and a voyage on the beautiful Natchez.

programme.desc: Join Ellen Coughlan as she explores the iconic city of New Orleans. Nicknamed the “Big Easy”, it’s known for its round the clock nightlife, vibrant live-music scene, and a spicy, singular cuisine… reflecting its history as a melting pot of French, African and American cultures. New Orleans is famous for its Mardi Gras, where parades and street parties fill the city. It’s also home to the iconic Natchez Steamboat, the last completely steam powered paddleboat on the Mississippi River. The second part features more food, some cocktail making and a voyage on the beautiful Natchez.

programme.title: Destination
programme.desc: Join John Plaskett as he discovers the vibrant history of the Italian city of Brescia. Home to several UNESCO World Heritage Sites this city has gone out of its way to preserve its colourful history. From the remains of Ancient Roman houses in the Santa Guila Museum Complex to the astronomical clock located in Piazza della Loggia. With every corner you turn there is more history looking back at you.

programme.title: Essence Of India
programme.desc:
Samira is in New York, getting ready for an exciting trip back home to India, where she re-visits Indian cuisine with her New York culinary trained eye. She packs her bags and sets off.
New York’s signature street food is the hot dog. In India, street food is a highly developed cuisine all on its own, going back hundreds of years. Samira has her own take on the shammi kabab and turns them into mini burgers in her kitchen, before traipsing all over New Delhi in her Essence of India auto rickshaw devouring the hearty Samosa, the succulent Kathi wraps, the moorishly moist Biryanis and even ends up taking over a street cart with a smorgasbord of sweet, tangy and spicy Indian chaat.

Samira has her own take on the shammi kabab and turns them into mini burgers in her kitchen, before traipsing all over New Delhi in her Essence of India auto rickshaw devouring the hearty Samosa, the succulent Kathi wraps, the moorishly moist Biryanis and even ends up taking over a street cart with a smorgasbord of sweet, tangy and spicy Indian chaat.

programme.desc:
The whole world loves a good curry, and living in New York, Samira loves to make curries, Indian, South East Asian and the Western stew, but she heads back to India where she learns how to make some of India’s finest curries.
Here is the story of ultimate deliciousness -- the tale of the curry. The desire to perfect her skills, sets her off on a curry trail, seeking out the best chefs in Delhi and getting them to spill their secrets.
This episode travels through the kitchens of master chefs, who created the king of all curries, The Butter Chicken, reintroduces the authentic korma, a recipe that has been tweaked across the globe and tells the story of the Raja Mirch, the hottest pepper in the world.

programme.desc: News - Movement may be one of the most powerful tools available for people living with multiple sclerosis. In this episode of Hope & Health, Mathew Embry speaks with Trevor Wicken, founder of The MS Gym, about how targeted movement training can help people with MS improve mobility, strength, and neurological function. The conversation explores neuroplasticity, foot drop, and the discipline required to stay consistent with movement when living with a neurological condition. Trevor also shares how a spinal injury at 16 shaped his philosophy and how two women living with MS ultimately changed the direction of his career and led to the creation of The MS Gym

The conversation explores neuroplasticity, foot drop, and the discipline required to stay consistent with movement when living with a neurological condition. Trevor also shares how a spinal injury at 16 shaped his philosophy and how two women living with MS ultimately changed the direction of his career and led to the creation of The MS Gym

Diagnosed in 1996, Bill shares how his medical background and personal experience shaped his long-term approach to managing MS. The conversation explores hyperbaric oxygen therapy, omega-3 supplementation, the microvascular theory of MS, and the role of blood flow and cellular energy in neurological health. Bill also reflects on discipline, daily habits, and why many of the strategies he uses extend beyond MS to broader brain and recovery science.

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E03 - Cunning Copulation
programme.desc: Finding a mate, building a nest, and raising kids are all part of the whole reproductive behavior thing. But it’s not as easy as it sounds. First, you’ve got to sift through lots of possible partners to find the one with the best genes to keep your family line going. Nesting involves finding some space and then guarding it fiercely, while raising the little ones takes loads of energy as you have to feed, teach, and keep them safe until they grow up. This episode dives into the ins and outs of how creatures go about their reproductive business.

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E03 - Cunning Copulation
programme.desc: Finding a mate, building a nest, and raising kids are all part of the whole reproductive behavior thing. But it’s not as easy as it sounds. First, you’ve got to sift through lots of possible partners to find the one with the best genes to keep your family line going. Nesting involves finding some space and then guarding it fiercely, while raising the little ones takes loads of energy as you have to feed, teach, and keep them safe until they grow up. This episode dives into the ins and outs of how creatures go about their reproductive business.
programme.sub-title: Survive the Wild - S01:E03 - Cunning Copulation

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E05 - Masters of Attack
programme.desc: Carnivores can't just pick their meals off trees. To survive, they have to use every trick they've got to catch food that's just as keen on staying alive as they are. If their prey hides, they have to find it. If it runs, they must chase it. They have to track it if it's hard to pin down and beat it if it fights back. The predator might use its strength for the final blow, but the real effort lies in the strategy.

programme.desc: The game wardens are on a mission to find a possible poacher who hunted a deer before the season started. Meanwhile, another warden is taking his son on a hunting trip after his son scored a rare moose tag.

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E06 - Devious Defenses
programme.desc: Animals can employ a number of different defenses in order to withstand an attack. Some seek safety in herds, some hide in plain sight, some meet aggression with even stronger aggression, and some build fortresses. Whatever the strategy it is clear that animals will do whatever it takes to survive the wild.
programme.sub-title: Survive the Wild - S01:E06 - Devious Defenses

programme.title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E05 - North Coast and Seat Belt
programme.desc: Game Wardens take on one of the biggest cases ever in Ohio's Division of Wildlife's 146-year history. They must figure out what happened when a bunch of people break the law. In "Seat Belt," a routine traffic stop leads to a surprising find.
programme.sub-title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E05 - North Coast and Seat Belt

programme.title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E06 - Lobster Poaching and Black Walnut
programme.desc: In "Lobster Poaching," a poacher has a bad day by jumping into the wrong boat. Meanwhile, "Black Walnut" tells a story about a surprising species that catches a Game Warden's attention. Game Wardens reminisce about unforgettable cases and experiences from their jobs.
programme.sub-title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E06 - Lobster Poaching and Black Walnut

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E04 - Elizabeth At 80 Continuity And Change
programme.desc: Thanks to the Queen’s dedication, Britain found a way to move past its empire days and create a successful new identity, surprising many experts. This is the story of an amazing woman and her amazing life.
programme.sub-title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E04 - Elizabeth At 80 Continuity And Change

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E08 - Princess Diana The Uncrowned Queen
programme.desc: This show offers a captivating look into the extraordinary life of one of the 20th century's most fascinating women, seen through an American lens. It features clips from the auction where her dresses were sold.
programme.sub-title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E08 - Princess Diana The Uncrowned Queen

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E09 - Queen Camilla
programme.desc: The documentary Queen Camilla? takes a closer look at Camilla Parker-Bowles, covering her history, her life, and what lies ahead. It focuses on her long standing ties with Prince Charles. The film also delves into the drama around Camilla's role in Prince Charles's marriage to Princess Diana.

programme.title: Dropped - S05:E09 - Head to Head
programme.desc: With the arctic storm nipping at their heals, the Keefer brothers race down the river to reach their next supply-yielding cache only to become lost as the river divides into a maze of small channels.

programme.title: Dropped - S05:E10 - Edge of the Storm

programme.title: Fight to Survive - S03:E04 - Treestand Nightmare
programme.desc: When avid bow hunter, Dr. Joe Baumgardner sets out to do routine maintenance on his tree stands, a twenty two foot fall leaves him with a severely broken leg and miles from help in the deep Mississippi woods.
programme.sub-title: Fight to Survive - S03:E04 - Treestand Nightmare

programme.title: Fight to Survive - S03:E05 - Crushed by a Boulder Part 1
programme.desc: While solo climbing Mt. Goddard, a remote peak in the California Sierra, Gregg Hein's leg is crushed by a boulder and he's sent careening down the mountain. Barely able to stop his fall, he's now faced with a horrific compound fracture.
programme.sub-title: Fight to Survive - S03:E05 - Crushed by a Boulder Part 1

programme.title: Fight to Survive - S03:E06 - Crushed by a Boulder Part 2
programme.desc: After his leg is crushed by a boulder, Gregg Hein is stranded on a high Sierra peak with an infected compound fracture. Knowing he won't be reported missing for days, Gregg attempts to crawl off the mountain and rescue himself.
programme.sub-title: Fight to Survive - S03:E06 - Crushed by a Boulder Part 2

programme.title: Fight to Survive - S03:E07 - Iraqi Sniper Attack
programme.desc: On deployment in Anbar Province, Marine Corp Master Sergeant Buck Doyle throws himself in harms way to save a fallen comrade from an Iraqi sniper and becomes a target himself.
programme.sub-title: Fight to Survive - S03:E07 - Iraqi Sniper Attack

programme.title: Fight to Survive - S03:E08 - Lightning Strike
programme.desc: A bass fishing trip goes horribly wrong when a bolt of lightning strikes their boat, leaving Seventeen-year-old Christian Neal burned and unconscious and his father Gabe blown into the water and paralyzed. It will take a miracle to save them.
programme.sub-title: Fight to Survive - S03:E08 - Lightning Strike

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E01 - Rules of the Realm
programme.desc: Animals or groups protect their territory by using sounds like birds singing or scents like pheromones from many mammals to mark boundaries. These are just the initial warnings. If other animals ignore these signs, a conflict might happen. Animals need a secure territory to mate, raise their young, and ensure there's enough food and resources for survival. This episode looks at the strategies animals use to claim their territory.
programme.sub-title: Survive the Wild - S01:E01 - Rules of the Realm

programme.title: Survive the Wild - S01:E02 - Nature's World Wide Web
programme.desc: When animals share info to help each other decide, it's called animal communication. They use stuff like sounds, colors, body language, movements, electric signs, touches, smells, or a mix of these. Whether it's a sea anemone spreading its tentacles or a male lion considering approaching a mate, their skill in communicating can be vital for their success. This episode dives into how animals interact with one another.
programme.sub-title: Survive the Wild - S01:E02 - Nature's World Wide Web

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E11 - Royal Children Prince William and Prince Harry
programme.desc: Two young men who have had to cope with extraordinarily challenging events and circumstances as, together, they have gone on to change the face of the British royal family and carve meaningful roles for themselves in the modern world. programme.sub-title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E11 - Royal Children Prince William and Prince Harry

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E12 - The New Royals
programme.desc: Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie have gone through a lot of media attention and tough situations in their lives. Through serving the Commonwealth, both sisters continue to make a positive impact.
programme.sub-title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E12 - The New Royals

programme.title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E01 - Introduction to Military Special Forces
programme.desc: “Special Operations” are special divisions of military, police or intelligence services that are highly qualified in specific areas of urban warfare and in a variety of special weapons and technology.
programme.sub-title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E01 - Introduction to Military Special Forces

programme.title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E02 - Introduction to Police Special Operations
programme.desc: As warfare has evolved, many military techniques and technologies have been adapted for use in urban settings by police units around the world. This episode provides viewers with an intimate perspective on what it feels like to be “inside the heads” of special police personnel, and how their use of military-style strategies and equipment allows them to save lives. From riot control in South Africa and the lessons learned from its excesses, to Los Angeles Police Chief Robert Gates’ creation of an elite police S.W.A.T team, CQB will showcase how, over the past 30 years, the fight against urban crime has evolved into a military scenario, with both sides using increasingly complex weaponry and tactics.
programme.sub-title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E02 - Introduction to Police Special Operations

programme.title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E07 - Game Camera Identifier and Living Rock Cactus
programme.desc: In 'Game Camera Identifier', a web of poachers are caught on camera. In 'Living Rock Cactus', a poacher is outed by succulent enthusiasts with watchful eyes. Game Wardens share past stories and details of notable investigation from their careers.
programme.sub-title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E07 - Game Camera Identifier and Living Rock Cactus

programme.title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E08 - Turtle Smugglers and Wire Fraud
programme.desc: In "Turtle Smugglers," they tell the surprising story of a big smuggling operation for these slow reptiles. "Wire Fraud" shares a sad story about getting scammed on social media. Game Wardens talk about old stories and memorable investigations from their work.
programme.sub-title: Wardens Case Files - S01:E08 - Turtle Smugglers and Wire Fraud

programme.title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E03 - Russian Army in Chechnya
programme.desc: After the fall of the soviet union many countries remained in dispute in the early nineties despite eastern Europe‘s independence. In 1994 a bitter conflict broke out between the forces of the Chechen independence movement and the Russian regular army. Despite overwhelming manpower, weaponry and air support, the Russian forces were unable to establish effective permanent control over the mountainous area due to many successful Chechen guerrilla raids. Improvised Explosive Devices were one of the most effective methods employed in these disastrous raids and were the back drop to many Close Quarter Battle scenarios exchanged between the two sides.
programme.sub-title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E03 - Russian Army in Chechnya

programme.title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E04 - SAS in Northern Ireland
programme.desc: The history of the British Empire colonial legacy in Northern Ireland is well known the world over but a there is a largely untold story of the the firefights between and close quarter battles exchanged between the provisional IRA, the British army and the elite SAS. Although the IRA often employed „terrorist“ techniques within the city of London and on England‘s mainland not much is said of the often guerilla warfare techniques of the British Special Air Service in Northern Ireland since the beginning of this conflict. In this episode we will examine how the history of the Special Air Service affected the training of every elite force after it and how the close quarter battles in Northern Ireland in the late 1970s through to the millennium shaped both special forces and resistance methods.
programme.sub-title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E04 - SAS in Northern Ireland

programme.title: Wardens - S04:E14 - Sullivan Hill

programme.title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E05 - Delta Prison Rescue Operation
programme.desc: In 1989, CIA operative Kurt Muse was imprisoned at the notorious Carcel Modelo in Panama for his role in organizing radio transmissions against dictator Manuel Noriega. That December, an elite group of the US Delta Force breached the roof of the prison, and one of the most daring close quarter battle operations in history began. From the dramatic helicopter crash and wounding of several Delta operators to the extraction of the entire team by the 5th Infantry Division, this is prime material for CQB analysis. In this episode, CQB recreates the raid, focusing on the “sub-second” reflexes of the Delta Force team from the moment they entered the prison to their extraction from the roof of the prison by an MH-6 “Little Bird” helicopter.
programme.sub-title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E05 - Delta Prison Rescue Operation

programme.title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E06 - Snipers and Scout
programme.desc: Joint Task Force Two (JTF 2) is the elite Canadian Forces Special Operations unit responsible for a broad range of missions, including counter-terrorism and armed assistance to other government departments. Highly secretive, JTF 2 and its predecessor, the Canadian Airborne Regiment, have been deployed in hotspots around the world from Haiti to Bosnia. This episode focuses on the legendary JTF sniper teams and their use in Afghanistan alongside the British SAS and the US Delta Force at “the sharp end of the spear.” A book written by an ex-JTF member explains how, in 2006, both the Pentagon and the British Foreign Office noted the instrumental role that JTF 2 played in the rescue of the British and Canadian Christian Peacemaker Team held hostage in Iraq. Unique in look, the FN P90 personal defense weapon, used by JTF 2 soldiers and special police around the world, will be highlighted in this program.
programme.sub-title: Close Quarter Battle - S01:E06 - Snipers and Scout

programme.title: Carter's W.A.R. - S01:E01 - Rhino Wars
programme.desc: Carter's W.A.R. (Wild Animal Response) is the untold story of one man's quest to save his homeland, the world's most wild and dangerous continent on earth, Africa. From heavily armed poachers butchering elephants for their tusks to the slaughter of rhinos for their horns, Africa's most precious resource is in peril. Can one man expose the truth and make a difference? Watch as wildlife detective and professional hunter, Ivan Carter, takes you inside the real Africa to the front lines of the wars being waged on its wildlife.
